Listen to this article Share The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) has appointed eight pre-shipment inspection agents and two monitoring and evaluation agents for crude oil and gas exports, while reallocating export terminals among the companies under the Nigerian Export Supervision Scheme. The appointments and terminal allocations, announced in a circular dated October 29, 2026, and signed by Aderinola Shonekan, director of the CBN’s Trade and Exchange Department, took effect from October 2, 2026. The revised arrangement covers major crude oil and gas export terminals across the country, with the CBN directing authorised dealer banks, the Nigeria Customs Service, petroleum regulators, the Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation Limited, terminal operators and oil and gas companies to ensure compliance. Under the new allocation, Dakee Engineering and Construction Limited will handle liquefied natural gas (LNG), Escravos (Gas), Bonny River Terminal and EGTL. Trexem Energy Services Limited has been assigned Egina, Qua-Iboe and Tulja terminals, while Geoscape Limited will oversee Escravos, ERHA, Odudu and FSO Cawthorne. The CBN allocated Bonga, Brass, Usan and Eagle terminals to 617 Limited, while Robinson International Energy Limited will cover Ugo-Cha, Penington, Aje, Ima, Oyo and Nembe. Trobell International Nigeria Limited has been assigned Forcados, Bonny and Okwori terminals, while Integrated Shipping Services Nigeria Limited will handle Akpo, Antan, Okoro, Anyala-Madu and Ebok. Kephren Business Limited will oversee Ukpokiti, Utapate, Yoho, Abo, Agbami, Ajapa, Okono and Okwok terminals, as well as additional marginal streams designated by the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC). The apex bank also appointed Q&Q Control Services Limited and Arlington Securitas Nigeria Limited as monitoring and evaluation agents responsible for supervising the inspection companies. Q&Q Control Services Limited will monitor the activities of 617 Limited, Trexem Energy Services Limited, Geoscape Limited and Kephren Business Limited. Arlington Securitas Nigeria Limited will oversee Dakee Engineering and Construction Limited, Trobell International Nigeria Limited, Robinson International Energy Limited and Integrated Shipping Services Nigeria Limited. The appointments form part of the Federal Government’s review of the pre-shipment inspection and monitoring arrangements for crude oil and gas exports under the Nigerian Export Supervision Scheme. The CBN directed all affected institutions and operators to comply with the revised appointments and terminal allocations, which it said took effect on October 2, 2026.
